title: Manual overview, purpose, scope, and document control — controlled evidence plan
purpose: Define the controlled manual architecture, document hierarchy, versioning, applicability, authority and release-state rules for the cultivation SOP system.

excludedUntilApproved: claim that a generic quality framework is cannabis law
silent retroactive revision of historical requirements
use of draft/internal-preview material as an effective operational SOP
uncontrolled local copies treated as authoritative

claims.statement: A controlled SOP system should make purpose, scope, responsibilities, prerequisites, required steps, records and exception/escalation paths clear enough that authorized users can execute and audit the process consistently.
claims.boundary: The exact required structure may differ by organization or jurisdiction; the SOP architecture must remain subordinate to applicable law, contracts and facility governance.

claims.statement: Only the effective controlled version should govern current work, while historical versions must remain traceable so past events can be reconstructed against the instruction that was actually in force.
claims.boundary: A later revision can guide corrective action but must not be rewritten into the past as if it governed earlier work.

claims.statement: Document changes should preserve who changed what, when, why, review/approval status and effective date so process evolution remains reconstructable.
claims.boundary: The educational framework does not prescribe one software platform or electronic-signature implementation.

claims.statement: Background science, training explanation and operational execution instructions should be linked but distinguishable so required steps are not buried in educational narrative.
claims.boundary: Separating execution from background does not mean workers should be trained without understanding the scientific basis.

claims.statement: Controlled procedures should identify the forms, logs, checklists or electronic records needed to capture critical observations, decisions, deviations and approvals.
claims.boundary: A field should not be added merely to create paperwork; records should support a defined operational, quality, safety or traceability purpose.

claims.statement: Jurisdiction-specific rules, product labels, equipment manuals and approved facility procedures override generic educational examples when they impose more specific requirements.
claims.boundary: Transferable quality standards must not be presented as jurisdiction-specific cannabis regulation.
